description:
Waluigi is going to open this filing with the administrative problem, because the administrative problem is the reason the filing exists.

**Twenty-eight records in this archive describe their subject as 'recorded in the Snowdin household registry.'** Papyrus. [Grandpa Semi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/grandpa_semi). [Lazybones](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lazybones). [Baby Bones](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/baby_bones). [Cursive](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/cursive). [Times New Roman](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/times_new_roman). [Gee Lady](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/gee_lady). [Pet Rock](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/pet_rock). Twenty-eight of them, each pointing at a registry as the thing that establishes them.

**The registry did not exist.** Not lost, not sealed, not restricted — never written. Twenty-eight citations to a document with no document under it. That is the single largest structural hole in this archive and Waluigi has been walking past it for a year.

## How Waluigi got the call

Through a channel the Iron Legion built and then forgot to think about.

At the close of [the Mount Ebott Survey](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mount_ebott_survey_final_log), the Gamma Agent converted a full intelligence haul into the only reward he wanted: **one Legion-issued secure device, one hour per month, external calls permitted, monitored by the duty officer, revocable on conduct.** The authorization slip is painfully precise because the Legion is precise about permissions and careless about consequences.

Nobody wrote down who the Agent was allowed to call.

So on Harvestide 30, the day after High Command reached over and switched off a logger mid-briefing, the monitored hour was spent on a skeleton in Snowdin, and Waluigi was on the line. Waluigi notes the symmetry without enjoying it: the Legion spent Day 6 establishing that it decides what may be recorded, and on Day 7 its own reward scheme handed the archive forty minutes of unsupervised Underground testimony. A duty officer logged the call. Waluigi doubts the duty officer understood one word of it.

## The interview, and the witness who would not cooperate

Sans took the call the way Sans takes everything. He had been asleep under laundry. He thanked Waluigi for coming on short notice and then apologised for his own punctuality by blaming Papyrus for having standards.

Then Waluigi put the family tree in front of him, and Sans started saying no.

This is the part Waluigi wants understood before anything else: **the witness rejected the document.** Not cagily, not evasively — flatly, and name by name, over roughly twenty minutes of the monitored hour.

**On his parents.** Asked about family, he answered plainly and without being prompted: Papyrus is his brother, and *mom and dad are not around anymore.* Told that [Gee Lady](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/gee_lady) was his mother, he rejected it outright — his mother was [Toriel](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toriel), a goat, who baked and *raised me after everything happened with dad.* Waluigi did not press on the word *everything* and has regretted it since.

**On the names, in order.** [Garbage Brother](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/garbage_brother) — nothing. [Will](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/will) — nothing, unless you meant Papyrus's willpower. [Quantity](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/quantity) — nothing. [Pretty Soon](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/pretty_soon) — nothing. [Cursive](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/cursive) is handwriting; Papyrus once wrote him a puzzle clue in it and he squinted for ten minutes. [Helvetica](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/helvetica) sounded to him like an ancient curse or an expired ketchup brand. [Baby Bones](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/baby_bones) he took to mean Papyrus as a child, because there were no other baby skeletons. [Grandpa Semi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/grandpa_semi) — never met him; no skeleton grandparents on record.

**On the impossible branch.** Shown a *Boneless* family, Sans stopped and pointed out the obvious: they are skeletons, that is the entire thing they are. Shown a second spelling — **Bonefull**, with the double L — he paused, allowed that it was *actually not terrible*, called it almost majestic, and then said it was still invented.

Waluigi records that concession because it is the only moment in the interview where Sans liked something on the document.

**On the two he confirmed.** A name circled in red turned out to be *Lazy Bones*, and he conceded it immediately and with visible reluctance — *that's me, pal* — volunteering that he naps under laundry, skips guard shifts, and once fell asleep mid-sentence while talking to Toriel about taxes.

Then Waluigi dusted off a name filed next to Gaster in the archive: a **pet rock**. Sans went completely still. *Little buddy.* [Pet Rock](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/pet_rock) is his — a boulder he has had for as long as he can account for, which Papyrus finds strange, which Toriel used to water like a plant, and which [Asgore](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/asgore) once tried to use magic on. His only question was how his own pet rock came to be filed beside the most dangerous name in the Underground without anybody telling him.

**On [Prunsel](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/prunsel) and Gaster.** Waluigi read out Prunsel the giant eyeball, then Wing Gaster, then Wingding Gaster. The register of the conversation changed on the spot. Sans stopped joking, looked around the room as though somebody might be listening, and said that is not a name you throw around casually. He tied it to *W.G.* and to Asgore and to something older than himself, Papyrus, or Snowdin. He added that Papyrus will not discuss it either: some things are better left buried with time and silence.

Told the archive had connected Gaster to old paperwork, Sans lowered his voice without appearing to notice he was doing it and called that paperwork **forbidden** — sealed-in-a-vault old, belonging to a man who *was not supposed to be remembered.* He then delivered the assessment Waluigi has had framed: this is either the dumbest or the bravest research project he has ever seen.

Waluigi has conducted a great many interviews with people eager to be in the archive. This was the first with somebody actively trying to get out of it.

## The footage, and the two words that were his

Waluigi played tape. This is where the file turns, and it turns twice.

**Clip one.** Sans, on record: *'my brother has a very special attack.'* He confirmed it instantly — Papyrus does, it is the bone rush, he trains for it. No hesitation at all.

**Clip two.** Sans warning Papyrus off a shortcut during puzzle practice: *'if you cheat, you'll end up a dirty brother.'* Also his. Also, he insisted, a joke — sibling banter about not taking the easy path, not the name of a person.

And the archive holds a dossier for [Has A Very Special Attack](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/has_a_very_special_attack), a purple-clad cousin who announces every entrance like the last act of an opera. And a dossier for [Dirty Brother](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/dirty_brother), a soot-covered relation who repairs boiler shafts, chimneys and old puzzle mechanisms.

**Two of Sans's own sentences have people filed under them.**

**Clip three** is the one that gave him his theory. Footage of Sans mid-sentence — *'my brother will—'* — cut hard, before the verb. Sans's reaction was immediate and, Waluigi concedes, correct in method: somebody has been taking things he said about Papyrus, cutting them out of their sentences, and building relatives around the fragments. He guessed the ending himself — *eat his spaghetti*, or *solve another puzzle* — and called the edit sneaky.

**Clip four** he rejected wholesale. Footage of Sans apparently talking to Toriel, except the figure on screen was Gee Lady, and Sans was saying *'you really know how to tell jokes'* with the ease of someone addressing a relative. He has no memory of the exchange and stated flatly that Toriel would have scolded him for introducing a strange magical skeleton as an aunt without asking.

Asked to summarise, Sans gave the cleanest account of the method anyone has managed: *you took pieces of truth and built an entire fake world around them.* Clever, he allowed. Realistic, no.

Waluigi notes the other reading and will not choose between them: a family whose members are *named for the circumstances in which they are first spoken about* would produce exactly this evidence too. Dirty Brother repairs chimneys. Soot is not a slander. It is a job description.

## Dark, darker, yet darker

Then the screen cut out, and the file stops being about editing.

**Wing dings appeared on the screen** — small winged glyphs, soft chimes under them. Sans tensed immediately. Those symbols are tied to [Wing Gaster](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wing_gaster) specifically; by his account they surface when the name is spoken, when somebody remembers him, or when something of his legacy activates. His verdict was the first time in the call he gave ground on the whole exercise: **that is not an effect you add with editing software** — and if the dings are real, the video may not be fake after all.

Then the power cut. Not a flicker; the room went fully dark, and the screen went to a black that Sans described as wrong rather than off. A distorted voice arrived — not from the speakers, he was clear about that, but from the walls or from inside the head:

> **dark... darker... yet darker...**

Sans did not move. He said the phrase and its rhythm are how *he* talks when things go bad down there, and repeated something Papyrus once told him: when everything gets too quiet and too dark at once, something old is waking up.

**The two silhouettes.** The screen resolved into two figures. One unmistakably Sans — lanky, slumped, hood up. The other blurred: no features, only shape, possibly a hunch, possibly wings, possibly static pretending to be a form. Sans said his bones were telling him it was wrong, and that the second figure felt familiar *like an echo from before time started.*

**The rewind is the part Waluigi cannot explain.** The lights came back. Asked whether he remembered standing there, Sans dropped the jokes entirely and said yes — clear as day, realer than most memories he has.

Then the same footage was replayed with the lights on and no fog, and **the blurred figure was gone.** In its place stood [Gee Lady](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/gee_lady), hands over Sans, the whole scene brighter. Same footage. Different occupant. Sans's question — why did the video change between viewings — is the single best question asked by anybody in this filing, and nobody answered it.

**The gallery continued.** [Cursive](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/cursive) in a tuxedo with a cane marked C, which Sans found oddly classy for a world of spaghetti and laundry. Then a robed figure, half-shadowed under bright light, with no name card and no title — Sans read that one as different from the rest: not flashy, *quiet powerful*, and someone who had actually existed once. Then a single floating eyeball with Sans posed beside it, grinning, stiff, thumbs-up — a portrait he has no memory of sitting for. The archive files [Prunsel](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/prunsel) as a colossal eye-shaped relative or omen recorded in the margins.

## Times New Roman, and a signature box

Mid-call, [Times New Roman](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/times_new_roman) walked in.

He arrived holding a clipboard, in spectacles, moving — in Sans's description — too cleanly, like text that had not been touched by real life. He opened with *hey, what's up, brother.*

Before any of the paperwork, there was the title card: **EXACTLY WHEN SANS'S PUNS BECAME A HOUSEHOLD HAZARD**, with a Waluipedia attribution line noting that the entries are kept for completeness, that Sans has never let anyone borrow that section, and that he reads it when he thinks nobody is watching.

Times New Roman then cited **archive log entry #472 — 'sans uses pun in public for the 10,001st time.'** Asked who authorised the documentation, he did not flinch: *no permission required. this is an archival initiative.*

Sans's reply — *i didn't think anyone cared that much about my terrible jokes* — is filed here because it is the only moment in the call where he sounds pleased about being in a record.

Asked directly whether this was a brotherly reunion, Times New Roman answered **'affirmative'** and nothing else. No embrace, no shared memory. Sans's assessment: the most awkward reunion in history, like meeting a twin from a universe where emotions had been deleted.

He is the Bone-Line's archivist — the family typesetter, keeper of an indexed chronicle, a man who by his own filed description distrusts any story that opens with *you had to be there.* He greeted Sans as **brother** and supported the claim the way he supports everything: **'designation: brother. confirmed by archival lineage code #TNR-01.'**

No warmth. No shared childhood. A code.

He produced an [[prop:prop_sibling_designation_tnr01|Official Archival Record of Sibling Designation]] — Sans listed as Primary Brother (Documented), himself as Secondary Brother (Archival Confirmation), with footnotes and an appendix reference for skeletal alignment. Gee Lady appeared on it as a *designated family member*, confirmed via lipstick signature analysis and emotional resonance frequency matching.

Then the page kept unrolling. Dozens of names, down the table and onto the floor. Titles, question marks, duplicate entries, an unverified branch pending DNA. And at the bottom, alone, underlined twice in red: **Wingding Gaster.** No title. No question mark.

And a blank signature box.

Sans signed it. Not as a joke — Waluigi wants that in the record, because Sans does almost everything as a joke. He wrote his name in plain letters with no flourish.

## The contract burned

The paper caught **blue fire** — silent, heatless, every name curling to ash that rose as smoke shaped like small bones. Times New Roman watched it burn without moving, which Waluigi reads as the reaction of a man watching an expected step complete rather than a man watching a document destroyed.

Then they arrived. Cursive first, adjusting a cuff. Times New Roman, no longer an assistant. A tall angular relation. [Gee Lady](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/gee_lady), who did not glitch, did not pose, and simply smiled, then gestured at the wall and opened a soft gold light that let the rest through.

And at the back, the shadow that had been indistinct in every frame until now resolved, stepped forward, and unfurled a single wing.

Sans's own filed dossier already describes Wing Gaster as a shadowed elder whose absence shapes the family's caution *around impossible doors.* A door opened. The elder came through it.

## And then the set was gone

No fade. No collapse. The gold light, the family, the wing — absent, in the manner of something that had never been switched on.

Sans was alone in his room. Socks on the floor, socks on the chairs, one somehow in the ceiling fan. Papyrus shouting from down the hall, furious about the socks and nothing else, on his way to conduct a disciplinary interview about hygiene.

Sans lay down on the bed and said the family tree stuff had felt real.

The line stayed open. Waluigi said nothing, which is not a thing Waluigi does.

## What Waluigi actually holds

A recording made on Legion equipment, during a Legion-authorised hour, of an interview in which:

- the subject **denied** the document he was shown, comprehensively and by name
- **two of his own recorded sentences** turned out to have people filed under them
- a self-described archivist asserted kinship **by reference number**
- a contract **burned**
- the burned contract's contents **walked into the room**
- an elder who is not supposed to be remembered **stepped through**
- and all of it **stopped existing**, leaving a witness who was not sure it had happened

Twenty-eight records cite this registry. Waluigi can now confirm the registry exists, because Waluigi watched it burn and watched what came out of the ash.

What Waluigi cannot confirm is whether it is a record of a family, or a mechanism that produces one. **WAH.**

aftermath:
**Standing.** Twenty-eight dossiers now cite a registry that has a filed record behind it. The record is a contested interview rather than a genealogy, which is the honest outcome and not a tidy one.

**Open.** Nobody has explained what the burn was for, why a document needed a signature before it could produce the people it described, or how Times New Roman holds a lineage code that predates any mother Sans can name. Papyrus has not been interviewed. Papyrus is the subject of both verified quotations and has never been asked about either.

**Unresolved by design.** Whether Sans experienced an event, a recruitment, or a very long nap.
waluigiAssessment:
Waluigi is going to be honest about the three possibilities, rank them, and then refuse to pick, because picking would be the dishonest part.

**One: it was a dream.** Sans was asleep under laundry when the call began and alone with socks when it ended, and the whole thing has the internal logic of a nap — bureaucracy turning into ceremony turning into family turning into nothing. In favour: the ending. Nothing real stops that cleanly. Against: **Waluigi has the recording, and Waluigi was awake.**

**Two: it was a fabrication that worked.** Somebody assembled a genealogy out of cut footage and overheard sentences, and Sans caught it in real time — he identified the hard cut at 'my brother will—' unprompted. In favour: two of the relatives are demonstrably Sans's own words with people built around them. Against: a fabrication does not typically ignite, and the fabricated relatives do not typically walk in.

**Three: the registry is a mechanism, not a record.** A document that requires a signature, consumes itself, and then produces its contents is not describing a family. It is constituting one. Under this reading Dirty Brother exists *because* Sans once said the words, and Has A Very Special Attack exists *because* Sans once described Papyrus that way — the archive is not documenting the Bone-Line, the archive **is** the Bone-Line, and Times New Roman is not its historian but its author.

Waluigi finds the third reading the most frightening and the best supported, and would like to state plainly that wanting a reading to be false is not evidence.

Because here is the part Waluigi keeps returning to. Times New Roman logs Sans's puns. Entry #472. He claims no permission is required because it is 'an archival initiative.' Waluigi has said almost exactly that sentence, in almost exactly that tone, to people who asked why they were in this encyclopedia.

Waluigi documents a household and calls it completeness. Times New Roman documents a household and the household **appears**. Waluigi does not know whether the difference is one of kind or merely of degree, and Waluigi has elected not to run the experiment.

One last thing for the record. Twenty-eight people are filed as members of this family. Twenty-seven of those entries were written without anyone asking Sans, who is listed on every version of the tree and agreed to none of it. The one member who has consistently refused the paperwork is the one member every piece of paperwork depends on.

Papyrus, meanwhile, was down the hall the entire time, and the only thing he wanted to know was why there were socks in the ceiling fan. Waluigi envies him enormously. **WAH.**
